reviewer.method: Full main text read in consecutive non-truncated ranges 1–135 and 136–317, including bibliography/endmatter. components.note: All main text, including references and disclosures, read.

All seven CT/angiography panels a–g and arrow legends; aggregate illustrative vascular abnormalities cannot be assigned to an unnamed individual.
All eight lung histology panels a–h, staining, arrows and scale bars; remodelling, congestion, infarction, plexiform lesions, bronchial vessels and embolization material.
All four panels a–d including inset morphology, scale bar, thickened/dilated subpleural veins and intravascular embolization material.

patient_identity.statement: XII-1 is a male diagnosed with PAH at 8 years. Figure 1a establishes XII-1 as maternal uncle of XII-2; this patient is the index uncle.

genotype.statement: Table 1 reports c.413G>C, p.Arg138Pro and Figure 1a shows heterozygosity, matching coding/protein change and zygosity in the packet.
limitations: Methods prints NM_0022454.3, whereas the packet uses NM_022454.4. The apparent source accession typo is retained; exact transcript/genomic coordinate equivalence was not independently confirmed in this review.

segregation.statement: Figure 1a shows two affected males and two unaffected female heterozygotes in family XII, consistent with autosomal dominant transmission with incomplete penetrance.
limitations: Selected affected families do not estimate penetrance. Table 1 marks index inheritance ND; pedigree relationships support transmission context, but no raw Sanger traces or independent genotypes are held.

phase.statement: A single heterozygous candidate is reported; cis/trans phase between two candidate alleles is not applicable.
limitations: Parental origin is depicted by the pedigree but not independently genotyped in this audit.

causal_confidence.statement: Table 1 classifies c.413G>C/p.Arg138Pro as ACMG class 4 (likely pathogenic); the packet upgrades this to PATHOGENIC and labels CAUSATIVE/SOLVED.
limitations: This is a source-label classification mismatch, not a new ACMG adjudication. The study contains no new variant-specific functional assay or drug-rescue experiment.

limitations: No new clinical examination. Histological absence does not prove absence throughout the bronchial arterial system; blank cells are not negative findings.

limitations: Post-inference source audit with aggregate outcome exposure; not new experimental or clinical validation.
Figure 1a corrects an interim reading note that incorrectly called XII-1 and XII-2 brothers: they are maternal uncle and nephew. No such brother relationship is retained in the adjudicated record.
Eight distinct patient columns appear in Table S1, while Methods/Results describe eight samples from seven patients. The source denominator conflict is retained.
Abstract follow-up median is 47 months; Results says 46. Discussion refers to two class-3 patients although Results/Table 1 list three.

Table 2 has five patients with any haemoptysis; Results specifies four with recurrent haemoptysis and three requiring multiple embolizations. These are different endpoints, so five versus four alone is not a demonstrated contradiction. Abstract wording conflates the recurrent and repeated-embolization groups.
The cohort deliberately includes three ACMG class-3 variants and one obligate carrier. Aggregate severity does not establish individual variant pathogenicity.
No N1002K/BubR1 measurement or comparative drug-benefit evidence is provided by this paper.
